text: Basic cattle care (ការថែទាំគោ) centers on adequate forage/feed (ចំណីសត្វ), clean water (ទឹកស្អាត), shelter/shade, and daily observation. Cattle are ruminants, so their diet should be mostly fibrous feed (pasture, grasses, hay, crop residues), with added energy/protein/minerals only when forage doesn't meet needs. Wet-season (May-October) pasture is more abundant but mud, flooding, and waterlogging can reduce grazing access and contaminate feed. Dry-season forage availability and quality decline, so conserve suitable feed before animals visibly lose condition -- don't wait until they're thin. Clean water must be available reliably, especially in hot weather, since heat stress reduces feed intake. Observe appetite, rumination, manure, body condition, movement, breathing, coat, and behavior daily; a change from the animal's own normal is more useful than memorizing symptom lists. Introduce feed changes gradually -- sudden large amounts of concentrate or fermentable feed can cause digestive problems. Never feed moldy, rotten, or chemically contaminated feed. Rice straw is a useful but nutritionally limited feed -- do not treat it as a complete diet, especially for young, pregnant, or lactating animals. Do not assume every farmer has irrigated pasture, purchased feed, or specialized housing; start from locally available safe forage and crop residues, basing mineral/concentrate supplementation on the animal's actual condition and veterinary advice rather than a fixed recommendation. Do not assume a specific cattle breed for Preah Vihear -- ask the farmer what type they keep rather than guessing from location.
